ut_forgotten_trails.blurb: A quiet, out-of-the-way sport crag tucked into American Fork Canyon in the Wasatch, on limestone. It is a place for stronger climbers: of the 28 bolted lines, most fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a handful of 5.13s and only a couple of easier pitches, so beginners will find little here. The main wall faces northeast and catches sun through the morning, while the stretch of cliff beyond it stays shaded early. A short, steep side wall holds a few extra routes. Expect solitude compared with the busier faces across the canyon, and plan on a real uphill hike through talus to reach the base.

ut_millstone_the.blurb: The Millstone is a wall of short quartzite in Big Cottonwood Canyon, in the central Wasatch, reached by the trail toward Lake Blanche. Its 28 routes are a mix of bolted and gear-protected lines: mostly sport, with around ten trad. Climbing is on edges and sidepulls with pumpy moves, and the bulk of the grades sit at 5.10 to 5.11, with a few 5.12s and only a small number of easy routes, so it suits intermediate to strong leaders. The final stretch crosses very rough talus, which keeps casual visitors away and gives the cliff a remote feel, and the views from the tops are fine.

ut_storm_mountain_island.blurb: A freestanding block of quartzite beside the stream in Big Cottonwood Canyon, close to the road near the Storm Mountain picnic ground. It is one of the busier spots in the canyon and has a wide spread: mostly traditional routes, plus some sport lines, a pair of aid climbs and a few top-rope options. Grades run from 5.4 up through 5.13, with a large cluster between 5.5 and 5.10, so there is something for newer leaders as well as a few hard overhangs. Several multi-pitch lines exist. The stream is loud enough that talking to your partner can be difficult, so agree on signals before leaving the ground.

ut_flu_the.blurb: The Flu is a bouldering sector in the Right Fork of Joe's Valley, near Orangeville in central Utah, on sandstone. It is a newer area compared with the valley's classic zones. The 27 problems here run across nearly the whole range, from an easy problem or two through the V3 to V7 middle, and on to several V8 and V9 lines, so it favors climbers working hard grades more than those after a mellow circuit. Sandstone here is fragile when damp, and the area is prone to holding moisture, so give it time to dry after rain or snow before pulling on anything.

ut_fringe_walls.blurb: Fringe Walls is a cluster of four separate sandstone walls along the road in Indian Creek, southeast Utah, where Wingate cracks are the main attraction. Nearly all of the 27 routes are trad, mostly crack climbs in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with a single bolted line; the largest share sits at 5.10, with a good number of 5.11s and a few 5.12s. Several of the walls date to the early days of climbing in the Creek. The walls draw far fewer people than the famous roadside cliffs, which makes this a pleasant change of pace, though each wall has its own pullout, so expect a little driving between them.

ut_minimum_crag_the.blurb: A shady, gently overhanging sport wall in the Right Fork of Maple Canyon, central Utah, on the conglomerate the canyon is known for. The 27 bolted routes lean hard: roughly half sit at 5.12, with another handful at 5.11, and only a few easy lines in the 5.5 to 5.6 range, so it rewards fit climbers with quality, well-bolted pitches in the soft side of the hard grades. Sun reaches the face early in the morning and then it falls into shade, and in winter it stays dark. The walk from the road is short, a few minutes on a trail, and the wall can be seen from the path.
ut_minimum_crag_the.parking_note: A small pullout on the west side of the road, on the right when driving up the fork, holds about two cars. The trail to the crag starts there.

ut_warm_up_area.blurb: A small bouldering zone in the Right Fork of Joe's Valley, central Utah, on sandstone and visible from the road, so it is among the first stops as you drive up the fork. A couple of boulders hold most of the problems, one of them large and hollowed into something like a cave. Of the 27 problems, the majority are easy to moderate, running from V0 up through V6, with a few much harder outliers for projects. Landings are generally good, which suits a first session of the day. Sandstone loses strength when wet, so leave it alone for a couple of days after any rain or snow.
